anomalies.obs: The 3.3 V rail is drawn under two different net names that are never joined. The LDO output (REG2 pin 1) and the peripheral ICs (INA219 VS pin 4, PCA9685 VDD pin 28, both EEPROMs VCC, and all NAVCPeripherals VDD) sit on a net labelled "+3.3V". The two MCUs (FCC1 VDD pins 11/27/50/75 and VDDA via FB1; NAVC1 VDD and VDDA via FB2), their I2C pull-up resistors R9–R14/R28–R31, and the USB‑UART bridges U11/U12 sit on a separate net labelled "+3V3". No wire, junction, 0‑Ω link, or shared label connects "+3.3V" to "+3V3" on any sheet.
anomalies.exp: The specification describes a single 3.3 V rail: "An LD39200PU33R LDO, fed from the 5 V rail, produces 3V3 for 'MCUs and Sensors'" and "3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs". The LDO output must therefore be the same net as the MCU/USB/pull‑up supply.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: LDO output arrow and INA219 VS arrow both read "+3.3V"; note "3.3V 2A Regulator (MCUs and Sensors)"
FCC sheet: VDD/VDDA arrows and pull‑up resistors read "+3V3"; NAVC sheet and Connections sheet also read "+3V3"
3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: The "+3V3" net that powers the STM32H753 (FCC1), the STM32F405 (NAVC1), their VDDA/VCAP domains, the I2C pull‑ups and the CH330 USB‑UART bridges has no source, because the LD39200 only drives "+3.3V". The microcontrollers and debug interfaces would be unpowered and the board would not boot, while only the sensors/PWM/EEPROMs would see 3.3 V.

parsed.summary: The part identities and passive values match the specification, but the 3.3 V rail is split into two unconnected net names ("+3.3V" on the regulator/peripheral sheets and "+3V3" on the MCU/USB/pull‑up sheets), so the LDO does not actually supply the two MCUs — a deviation from the single‑rail design the spec describes.
